props.text: Practical technique taught at your own bench.
Switch between our four studio tracks to inspect what you will make, the equipment you will use and the skills you will carry home.
Wild leaven, stone-milled flour, and hearth baking.
Work directly with freshly milled regional wheat, spelt and rye to understand hydration, bulk fermentation and oven spring.
Compare bolted stone-ground flours, ash content and water absorption at the bench.
Schedule levain builds and ambient bulk fermentation around a real home or bakery day.
Tension boules and bâtards, cut clean expansion ears and bake on hearth stone.

props.alt: Baker hands scoring a flour-dusted sourdough boule with a wooden lame

props.text: Butter plasticity, clean folds, and open honeycomb crumb.
Learn tactile temperature control so dough and dry-churned cultured butter roll at identical resistance without tearing.
Mix relaxed overnight pastry doughs with balanced elasticity and extensibility.
Execute letter folds and book folds with uniform 4 mm sheeting on chilled marble.
Read wobble and layer separation before glazing and baking to deep amber flake.

props.alt: Pastry chef rolling golden cultured-butter croissant dough layers on a marble slab

props.text: Koji inoculation, wild brines, and cellar condiments.
Turn seasonal produce, heirloom legumes and orchard fruits into complex misos, garums, lacto-pickles and living vinegars.
Grow fragrant rice and barley koji in cedar trays and mash long-aged amino pastes.
Calculate salt percentages by total weight for crisp seasonal vegetables and krauts.
Balance acidity, oxygen exposure and cellar aging for restaurant-grade larder jars.

props.alt: Glass fermentation jars and stoneware crocks filled with wild botanicals and miso on oak shelves

props.text: Handmade pasta, stocks, emulsions, and hearth cooking.
Build complete seasonal meals from whole produce, slow broths, brass-cut pasta doughs and pan sauces.
Balance 00 flour, semolina rimacinata and rich egg yolks for laminated and extruded shapes.
Roast bones and aromatics, clarify stocks and mount glossy starch-and-butter emulsions.
Layer acidity, garden sorrel, charred alliums and finishing salts at the pass.

props.text: An unhurried rhythm from first weigh-out to the shared table.
Good fermentation cannot be rushed. We structure full-day and weekend benches around natural resting windows so learning feels calm, observant and thorough.
Arrive to warm espresso and your printed formula sheet. We start by tasting flours, checking fermentation temperatures and mixing the day’s primary doughs or brines.
While doughs bulk-ferment or crocks settle, the cohort gathers in the glasshouse dining room for a seasonal family-style lunch cooked from our cellar and ovens.
Load the steam decks, score and glaze final bakes, jar your living starters, and walk through how to adapt every timing and humidity step for a domestic kitchen.
Three connected rooms designed for flour, steam, and conversation.
Explore our converted mill building—from the stone-deck bakehouse and marble pastry benches to the botanical larder and glasshouse dining room.

props.text: Four benches. Tactile craft for the home and working kitchen.
Every syllabus balances scientific clarity—hydration percentages, pH, butter plasticity and salt ratios—with the sensory cues of smell, elasticity and crust color.

props.alt: Dark stone-milled rye and country sourdough loaves cooling on a wire rack

props.text: Country Leaven, Whole-Grain Hydration & Hearth Baking
Two full days dedicated to wild-yeast ecology, freshly milled regional wheat and rye, coil folding, cold retarding and baking with live deck steam or domestic Dutch ovens.
Test stone-milled Red Fife, Khorasan and dark rye; adjust hydration from 74% to 86% by tactile feel.
Maintain stiff and liquid starters, balance lactic versus acetic acidity and read aliquot rise.
Shape boules, bâtards and tin loaves; manage bottom heat, steam venting and crust caramelization.

props.alt: Warm flaky artisan croissants and seasonal fruit danishes on a handmade stoneware platter

props.text: Croissant, Cultured Butter Danishes & Orchard Galettes
Work at chilled marble stations to master butter encapsulation, uniform lamination turns, overnight cold-proofing and crisp fruit-filled viennoiserie.
Mix enriched levain-yeast doughs, plasticize 84% butter blocks, complete double and single folds without butter shattering, and rest laminated slabs.
Cut geometric triangles, pain au chocolat batons and knotted cardamon buns; control humidity during final proof so butter stays inside the honeycomb.
Koji, Miso, Wild Brines & Orchard Vinegars
An immersive full-day bench inside our botanical larder exploring microbial safety, enzymatic grain conversion, vegetable lacto-fermentation and vinegar mothers.
Steaming, cooling and inoculating heritage rice and barley; packing six-month sweet and twelve-month country miso crocks.
Precision 2% to 3.5% salt-by-weight calculations, anaerobic ceramic weights and seasonal botanical aromatics.
Building dual-stage cider and perry vinegars, toasted-grain shoyu infusions and non-alcoholic cellar shrubs.

props.alt: Cedar tray of white rice koji beside ceramic bowls of aged miso and pickled radishes
Hand-rolled garganelli and tagliatelle pasta nests dusted with semolina on a walnut pasta board

props.text: Handmade Pasta, Slow Broths & Hearth Sauces
Spend a Friday evening or Sunday session rolling laminated egg-yolk sheets, shaping cavatelli and garganelli, and cooking a multi-course seasonal meal around the hearth.
Knead elastic doughs by hand, rest without oxidation and sheet paper-thin sfoglia with a wooden mattarello.
Bind glossy pan sauces with starchy pasta water, cultured butter, aged sheep cheese and roasted bone broths.
Cook with braised chicories, chanterelles, garden sorrel, preserved lemon and cellar miso.
Compare all eight workshops across our four disciplines.

pages.title: About — Sorrel & Stone

props.text: A working bakehouse built for curious hands.
Founded inside a former grain warehouse in the Mill District, Sorrel & Stone brings bakers, pastry chefs, fermenters and home cooks around the same ash-wood benches.
Technique is best learned through your hands, not from across an auditorium.

Too many cooking classes reduce students to spectators watching a single demonstration mirror. At Sorrel & Stone, every student mixes their own levain, sheets their own butter block, inoculates their own koji tray and scores their own loaves at an individual station.

We keep cohorts to eight or ten people so we can pause when a dough feels tight, compare fermentation aromas across the bench and show how small shifts in water temperature or salt percentage transform the result.

props.alt: Wide interior view of the Sorrel & Stone teaching bakehouse with steam deck ovens and ash workbenches

props.text: Taught by working bakers, fermenters, and cooks.
Our four resident leads teach every cohort in person and remain available after your session when you are troubleshooting a starter or brine at home.

props.alt: Claire Vance, Head Baker & Grain Lead at Sorrel & Stone

props.text: After twelve years leading wood-fired and steam-deck bakeries, Claire teaches whole-grain milling, wild-leaven ecology and high-hydration hearth shaping.

props.alt: Mateo Solis, Fermentation & Larder Director at Sorrel & Stone

props.text: Mateo oversees our sixty-jar fermentation cellar, guiding students through koji propagation, heirloom bean misos, lacto-brines and botanical orchard vinegars.

props.alt: Hana Lindqvist, Pastry & Viennoiserie Instructor at Sorrel & Stone

props.text: Trained in Stockholm and Lyon, Hana specializes in naturally leavened viennoiserie, cultured-butter lamination and seasonal stone-fruit galettes.

props.alt: Julian Marsh, Seasonal Kitchen & Pasta Lead at Sorrel & Stone

props.text: Julian leads our Friday evening pasta tables and Sunday hearth feasts, focusing on hand-rolled regional pasta shapes, stocks and whole-vegetable cooking.
Good technique starts with honest raw materials.
We source directly from regional grain growers, stone mills, pasture dairies and orchards so students experience how living ingredients behave.
We mill organic Red Fife, Sonora white wheat, Khorasan and dark Danko rye within forty-eight hours of every bread and pasta bench.
Our fermentation crocks and pastry benches follow the harvest—from spring rhubarb and green walnuts to autumn quinces and winter chicories.
Lamination classes work exclusively with high-fat, slow-cultured butter blocks and raw milk cheeses from neighboring pasture dairies.

props.alt: Warm botanical larder room with wooden shelves of glass fermentation jars, vinegars and stoneware crocks

props.text: Sixty living starters, mothers, and aged misos.

Every student who completes a sourdough or fermentation bench leaves with splits from our house culture library—including our fourteen-year rye mother, white and barley koji spores, and unpasteurized cider vinegar starters.
If your starter ever stalls at home, bring a clean jar back to Mercer Lane during studio hours and we will refresh your culture from the mother crock.

We reply within one business day with confirmed seat availability for your chosen cohort date and a complete PDF syllabus.
Let us know any food allergies, midday lunch preferences or adjustable-height bench requirements before your cohort meets.

props.text: Thoughtful spaces for standing, seated prep, and allergen care.
Our ground-floor bakehouse, fermentation larder and conservatory dining room have step-free street access and wide aisles between workbenches.

Two stations in the bakehouse are equipped with height-adjustable prep tables and padded stools. While our bakehouse mills wheat and rye daily, our fermentation larder can be configured for gluten-free miso and brine sessions on request.
